item.title: Implement thread-safe ledger API from SPEC.md
item.brief: Implement ledger.py according to SPEC.md and add focused tests extending the basics in test_ledger.py. Preserve the documented API and handle every specified error and boundary case. Use only the Python standard library. Acceptance criteria: constructor validates dict input, nonempty string account names, and built-in integer balances in [0, MAX_BALANCE], rejects bools, accepts empty dict, and copies input; snapshots are independent copies. transfer validates built-in integer amount in [1, MAX_BALANCE] before account lookup; unknown accounts raise KeyError; insufficient funds and destination overflow return False without mutation; successful transfer returns True and conserves total; same-account transfer returns True exactly when funded, changes nothing, and still validates amount/account; all operations including snapshots are linearizable across threads, with no half-transfer snapshots and no deadlock for opposite-direction transfers. Add deterministic focused tests for validation, boundaries, failure atomicity, alias isolation, self transfer, conservation, and concurrency as appropriate, without external services, wall-clock calculations, or random inputs. Run the relevant tests and fix issues. Commit the completed work on the assigned local branch; do not push.

pr.body: `ledger.py` copies and validates constructor balances, validates transfer amount before account lookup, and protects transfer checks/writes and snapshot copies with one per-ledger lock. `test_ledger.py` covers invalid inputs and boundaries, failure atomicity, input/snapshot isolation, self transfers, conservation, and opposing-direction concurrency. Verified with `python -m unittest -v` (10 passed) and `git diff --check` (passed). No separate build or lint configuration is present. Review covered base 195584275c12599a4d2d0ade3bab0a7ea8a4ecb5 through head c5e99dba35b8fcbdb9949c2df9c50dd878e37249. Reviewer follow-up left open: add a direct concurrent snapshot-versus-transfer regression to detect future synchronization regressions. No other known risks or assumptions.

risk.why: Concurrency and locking determine correctness. One lock guards the transfer checks and writes and the snapshot copy; the 10-test suite, including simultaneous opposite-direction transfers with a bounded join, passes.
